query: hantavirus confirmed cases by nationality MV Hondius latest
answer: As of May 2026, there are 11 confirmed or probable hantavirus cases linked to the MV Hondius cruise ship, with patients from the Netherlands, United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and France. Three people have died, two confirmed from hantavirus. The outbreak is under investigation.

results.content:
Oceanwide Expeditions, the company that chartered the MV Hondius cruise, released a list of the nationalities of all the passengers and crew members aboard the ship. Two dozen nationalities were represented on the ship, which sailed through the Atlantic Ocean. Among the countries represented, passengers and crew from the Netherlands, the United States, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and Germany appear to have developed symptoms.

Below is what we know about the 11 confirmed or probable hantavirus cases aboard the ship based on information from the World Health Organization, countries' medical and government officials and coverage of the hantavirus outbreak linked to the MV Hondius Cruise.

### Case 1: 70-year-old Dutch man believed to be first victim and first casualty [...] Facebook

WASHINGTON — As of Thursday, there were 11 confirmed or probable cases of the Andes hantavirus, which spread on an Atlantic cruise ship, known as the MV Hondius.

The Andes strain is the only strain of the virus known to spread person-to-person. Typically, the virus is spread from exposure to rodents. Symptoms may take 4 to 42 days to spread.

[...] ### Case 8: British man suspected of contracting virus

A British man disembarked from the MV Hondius on April 14, in the British island territory of Tristan da Cunha. His symptoms began on April 28, including diarrhea and fever. His condition was last described as "stable."

### Case 9: French woman develops severe symptoms

A French passenger from the ship is in a Paris hospital with severe symptoms, as of Wednesday. According to an infectious disease specialist at the Bichat Hospital, the woman has been receiving blood through an artificial lung.

Dr. Xavier Lescure of the Bichat Hospital described her treatment as, "the final stage of supportive care," while speaking with the Associated Press.

# Hantavirus: confirmed cases by nationality

The cruise ship MV Hondius stopped at the Spanish island of Tenerife on its way back to the Netherlands (JORGE GUERRERO)

Here is a roundup of which countries have confirmed or probable cases of nationals infected by hantavirus after the outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius, according to the World Health Organization.

Among living patients, seven cases have been confirmed and an eighth is listed as "probable", according to the WHO, the UN health body and certain national health authorities.

In addition, three people have died, with two of those confirmed as having hantavirus and one probable case, the WHO said. [...] - Spain -

A Spanish passenger evacuated from the disease-stricken MV Hondius cruise ship has tested positive for hantavirus but was not suffering symptoms, Madrid's health ministry said late on Monday.

The passenger "received a positive result from a PCR test done on his arrival" at the Gomez Ulla military hospital in Madrid, where he was being kept in isolation, the ministry said. It added that the "final results will be known in the coming hours" and the other 13 Spanish evacuees had tested negative for the time being.

results.title: MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak - Wikipedia
results.content:
In April 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus infection caused by the Andes virus was identified on the Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius. There are eight confirmed cases and two suspected cases directly linked to the outbreak as of 13 May. There have been three deaths, two of which have been confirmed as caused by the Andes virus, the last on 2 May. The original passengers have now all disembarked and been evacuated; many are quarantined in their home countries. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has classified the outbreak as a "level 3" emergency response. The World Health Organization (WHO) has not declared a specific level of emergency response. [...] Wikipedia

## Switzerland

### Confirmed Case

Swiss authorities confirmed at least one hantavirus case connected to the outbreak.

The infected individual had reportedly traveled aboard the MV Hondius before later arriving in Switzerland. Public health officials initiated monitoring protocols and contact tracing for potential exposures.

This marked one of the first confirmed European cases directly linked to the cruise ship outbreak. (washingtonpost.comAttachment.tiff)

Attachment.tiff

## Spain

### Active Monitoring and Incoming Patients

Although Spain has not publicly confirmed large numbers of domestic infections, the country became heavily involved after agreeing to receive the ship near the Canary Islands.

Spanish authorities: [...] The outbreak, believed to involve the Andes strain of hantavirus, has triggered multinational contact tracing efforts after infected passengers traveled through multiple countries before the illness was identified.

While the World Health Organization continues to assess the global public risk as “low,” the number of countries involved in the investigation has steadily expanded.

Here is a breakdown of the countries that have already reported confirmed cases, suspected infections, monitoring operations, or direct outbreak involvement.

## South Africa

### Confirmed Cases and Deaths

South Africa became one of the first major international response centers after symptomatic passengers from the MV Hondius arrived from Saint Helena in late April 2026.

Authorities confirmed: [...] Authorities confirmed:

South African laboratories played a key role in identifying hantavirus as the likely cause of the outbreak. Samples analyzed there later prompted WHO notification under International Health Regulations procedures.

The country also coordinated emergency medical evacuations and international contact tracing connected to commercial flights departing Saint Helena. (who.int)

## The Netherlands

### Confirmed Fatal Cases

The Netherlands is considered central to the outbreak because the two earliest known fatalities were Dutch nationals.

Authorities confirmed:

# Worldwide race to trace passengers from hantavirus-hit cruise ship

Getty Images People wearing personal protective clothing disembark a plane. 

Health authorities across the globe are racing to trace dozens of people who disembarked from a cruise ship before an outbreak of hantavirus was detected, and anyone who has come into close contact with them since.

Five cases have now been confirmed, including three deaths, following an outbreak on the Dutch vessel MV Hondius, the World Health Organization has said.

The UN health agency also said the outbreak is not the start of pandemic like Covid six years ago, because this hantavirus strain spreads through "close, intimate contact". [...] Here is what we know about the countries affected so far:

 World map showing where cruise ship passengers are being monitored or receiving treatment. Countries shaded red include Canada, the United States, Tristan da Cunha, the United Kingdom, Spain, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Denmark, Germany, South Africa and Singapore. The ship’s route is traced from Argentina, where it departed on 1 April, stopping at St Helena (where 29 passengers left the ship), and heading to the Canary Islands, and showing the ship’s position on 8 May in the Atlantic. 

## UK

Three British nationals have suspected hantavirus.

Seven Brits disembarked the MV Hondius in St Helena on 24 April before the first confirmed case of hantavirus was reported on 4 May, with four remaining there. [...] ## Netherlands

Thirteen people on the ship are Dutch, including eight passengers and five crew members.

The three deaths so far include two Dutch nationals, a husband and wife. The woman tested positive for hantavirus and died in South Africa.

A Dutch woman was admitted to a hospital in Amsterdam after showing possible symptoms of a hantavirus infection, the country's health ministry said on Thursday.

Dutch broadcaster RTL said the woman was a stewardess at Dutch airline KLM, who had been in contact with a woman who died from a hantavirus infection in Johannesburg.

However on Friday, a WHO official told CBS News that she had tested negative for the virus.

## Philippines

Among the crew of the MV Hondius are 38 people from the Philippines.

## Singapore

The Southeast Asian city-state announced on Thursday that it has isolated and is monitoring two of its residents who were aboard MV Hondius in its government facility. Singapore’s Communicable Diseases Agency said it was notified on May 4 and May 5 that the two residents, aged 67 and 65, were on the ship when it departed Ushuaia in Argentina on April 1. Both disembarked early and were on the same Johannesburg-bound flight as one of the confirmed hantavirus cases on April 25.

“One has a runny nose but is otherwise well, and the other is asymptomatic,” the agency said of the isolated residents. The two individuals’ test results are pending, but the Singaporean agency says the risk to the general public in Singapore is currently low.

## South Africa [...] ## Denmark

The Danish Patient Safety Authority said in a statement on Thursday that one of its nationals was on the MV Hondius. The agency said the person, who is self-isolating, returned to Denmark at the end of April, has displayed no symptoms of illness, and has not been in close contact with any of the people from MV Hondius who later developed an infection.

## Germany

As of May 4, there were 8 reported German nationals on the MV Hondius, including one crew member. Among them was a female passenger who passed after falling ill. On April 24, a German national disembarked at St. Helena.

An asymptomatic German was evacuated on May 6, and will reportedly be brought to a hospital in Düsseldorf for testing after having contact with the German who died. [...] ## Argentina

The MV Hondius departed Ushuaia, a city in southern Argentina, on April 1. One person on board the ship was an Argentine national.

Hantavirus is endemic in Argentina, but infections in the country are on the rise. The Argentine health ministry on Tuesday reported 101 hantavirus infections since June 2025, which is roughly double the caseload recorded over the same period the previous year, per the Associated Press.

# Canadian from hantavirus-hit cruise ship tests positive

Reuters Man in full PPE talks to man and woman wearing blue plastic outer clothing and face masks at the entrance to a Menzies Aviation Boeing 767 plane.

A Canadian who sailed on the cruise ship MV Hondius which was hit by a hantavirus outbreak in April has tested positive for the disease, officials in the province of British Columbia say.

The individual, one of four people isolating on Vancouver Island after leaving the ship, had developed mild symptoms.

The province's senior health officer said the four had not had any contact with the public since arriving in Canada. [...] Officials say the risk of a major outbreak is very low.

Map showing the route of the cruise ship MV Hondius across the South Atlantic Ocean with a timeline of incidents. The ship departs Ushuaia, Argentina on 1 April. On 11 April, the first passenger dies at sea. The route continues north east toward Africa. On 24 April, the wife of the deceased passenger is flown from St Helena to South Africa. A marker near South Africa notes: 26 April, a woman dies in Johannesburg; 27 April, a second sick passenger is flown to hospital. On 2 May, another passenger dies onboard. On 3 May, the ship arrives at Cape Verde. A final note says the ship has arrived in Tenerife on 10 May. The route is shown as a red line with arrows and black dots marking key locations. [...] The case brings the total number of infections to 11, all among cruise passengers. Three people who travelled on the ship have died, with two confirmed to have had the virus.

"Clearly, this is not what we hoped for, but it is what we planned for," she said, quoted by national broadcaster CBC.
